validated_results.title: Fat, protein, and meat consumption and renal cell cancer risk: a pooled analysis of 13 prospective studies.
validated_results.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
validated_results.reason: Pooled analysis of primary data from 13 prospective cohorts examining red meat intake and incident renal cell cancer; a red meat-specific null finding is reported although no numeric estimate appears in the abstract.

extraction.design: Pooled analysis of prospective cohort studies

sample_size.excerpt: Results of several case-control studies suggest that high consumption of meat (all meat, red meat, or processed meat) is associated with an increased risk of renal cell cancer, but only a few prospective studies have examined the associations of intakes of meat, fat, and protein with renal cell cancer. We conducted a pooled analysis of 13 prospective studies that included 530,469 women and 244,483 men and had follow-up times of up to 7-20 years to examine associations between meat, fat, and protein intakes and the risk of renal cell cancer.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 530469 + 244483 = 774952

cases.excerpt: A total of 1,478 incident cases of renal cell cancer were identified (709 in women and 769 in men).

timing.excerpt: had follow-up times of up to 7-20 years

exposure_measurement.excerpt: All participants had completed a validated food frequency questionnaire at study entry.

cases.excerpt: Cases were 767 subjects with incident histologically confirmed RCC and controls were 1,534 patients in hospital for acute non neoplastic conditions.

effect_size.excerpt: The corresponding ORs were 1.34 (95% CI 0.87-2.07) in men and 0.67 (95% CI 0.38-1.18) in women, 1.91 (95% CI 0.85-4.31) in current smokers and 0.74 (95% CI 0.41-1.31) in never smokers, with no trend in risk with dose.
